subject: physics_2
question_text: Using dimensional analysis obtain an expression for the speed of sound waves in a medium.

mark_split.label: Dimensional formulas of B and ρ

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for this paper: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers, so neither check was run. Physics hand-checked: [B] = ML⁻¹T⁻² (bulk modulus = pressure), [ρ] = ML⁻³, so B/ρ = L²T⁻² = [v²]; hence v = K√(B/ρ). This is the Newton–Laplace form; the exact treatment gives K = 1.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order — the two quantities the speed depends on, their dimensional formulas, and the final expression.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Dimensional formulas
steps.mark_note: D.F. of B and ρ written
lines: The speed of sound v in a medium depends
on the bulk modulus B and the density ρ

lines.text: D.F. of ρ = ML⁻³ ; v = LT⁻¹

steps.margin_note: First mark. Name the two quantities and write both dimensional formulas.
steps.why: Sound is a pressure wave, so the elastic property of the medium (bulk modulus) supplies the restoring force and the density supplies the inertia — these two are the physical inputs.
common_mistakes: Using linear density μ — that belongs to the string formula. A bulk medium takes density ρ (ML⁻³).
Writing B with the dimensions of force. Bulk modulus is pressure: force per area, ML⁻¹T⁻².

recall.must_convey: That the speed of sound depends on the bulk modulus B (ML⁻¹T⁻²) and the density ρ (ML⁻³).
accept: depends on bulk modulus and density
B is ML inverse T minus two
reject: v equals K root B by rho

steps.memory_tip: Same pattern as the string: an elastic property over an inertia property. Here they are B and ρ.

steps.label: Combining the dimensions
lines: So v² matches B/ρ. Taking the square root:
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Show B/ρ = L²T⁻² before writing the root — the division IS the working.
steps.why: B/ρ is the only combination of the two inputs with the dimensions of speed squared; the dimensionless K cannot come from dimensions. The exact derivation gives K = 1, the Newton–Laplace formula.
common_mistakes: Writing v = K(B/ρ) without the square root — B/ρ has the dimensions of v², not v.
Dropping the constant K. A pure number can never come out of dimensional analysis.

recall.must_convey: That B/ρ has the dimensions of v², so v = K√(B/ρ) with K a dimensionless constant.
accept: B by rho gives L squared T minus two
v equals K root B over rho
square root of bulk modulus by density

steps.memory_tip: Elastic property over inertia property, under a square root — the one shape both speed formulas share.

insider_note: The examiner checks the same two things as in the string version — the correct pair of quantities and the square root with a stated constant K.
